title: Optimise Performance Guide
subheading: Here are some things you can do to optimise for low-end computers (e.g., Celeron N4000):

contents.Text: [[[strong:Settings -> Image -> Image Padding Mode:]]] Set this to [[[strong:Off]]] to stop any extra image padding from being rendered, which speeds up image load times and lowers CPU usage.
[[[warning:Note:]]] The downside is that images rendered will not be centred.

[[[strong:Settings -> Image -> Randomiser Options:]]] If you use [[[strong:Randomiser]]] as the Image Padding Mode, tick the [[[strong:GPU Effects]]]. They are disabled by default, but they are vastly faster than the CPU effects, so it is encouraged to use them.

[[[strong:Tip:]]] If you move to the GPU effects, it is a good idea to untick the [[[strong:CPU Effects]]] as well. If both are ticked, the randomiser picks from all of them, so you will get a mix of CPU and GPU effects.
[[[strong:Settings -> Image:]]] These settings control how much memory and processing each image uses:

rows: Effects run on a smaller copy, the cheapest option

contents.Text: [[[warning:Note:]]] Images may look softer if the window is enlarged afterwards (for example going fullscreen) until the next song loads.
[[[warning:Note:]]] [[[strong:Enable the source image for effects]]] is ignored while [[[strong:Fit images to the display size]]] is on.
For more information on these settings, see the [[[button:Image][/Main Window/Settings/Image]]] page.
If you want to reduce the performance hit even more, then turn off images altogether:
[[[strong:Settings -> Image -> Display album art while playing music:]]] Set this to [[[strong:Off]]] to stop all image processing/rendering altogether.
[[[strong:Settings -> Fonts:]]] If you have [[[strong:dynamic fonts]]] enabled, it is a good idea to enable fewer fonts.
Each font uses more memory, because it has to be fitted into memory. Fewer fonts means less memory, which helps if you are memory constrained.
